name: Philips Norelco

card.summary: The US brand of Philips electric shavers and grooming trimmers, used to keep a clean-shaven face or neat stubble and to groom body hair.

quick.overview:
Philips Norelco is the name Philips uses for its electric shavers and grooming tools in the United States. Shaving or trimming facial hair is one of the most common grooming steps, and an even shave or tidy stubble line is a basic part of a groomed face.

The brand began with Philips electric shavers made from 1939 and sold in the US from 1948. Outside the US the same shavers were sold as Philishave until 2006. No clinical research evaluates the brand's effect on appearance.
quick.how: Users shave dry or with the product's wet options, or use trimmers to keep stubble at a set length. Bodygroom models are used for body hair. Forum discussion on T Nation has covered shaving and body-hair grooming among lifters.
quick.risks: Electric shaving can cause skin irritation or razor-bump-type reactions in some people. Blades and heads wear and are replaced.

lead: Philips Norelco is the US brand name for Philips electric shavers and grooming products. People use them to shave or trim facial hair, a routine step in a groomed appearance, and body-hair models extend this to the chest and other areas.

Philips began making electric shavers in 1939; World War II delayed the US launch to 1948, and sales took off after a two-headed model in 1951 [1]. A 1943 court ruling stopped Philips from using its own name in the US because of the Philco trademark, so it adopted Norelco, short for North American Philips Electrical Company [1]. Outside the US, Palau, Micronesia and the Marshall Islands, the shavers carried the Philishave name until 2006 [1].
The brand's product list has included the Compact Travel Razor (1997) and the Bodygroom (2006) [1]. No clinical studies examine the shavers' effect on appearance.

chain: Cuts facial hair to a chosen length or clean finish
Neat beard line or smooth face
angle.text: An electric shaver or trimmer gives a clean-shaven face or evenly kept stubble, and body-hair models groom other areas. The look is temporary and maintained by regular use.

paras: Philips shaver production started in 1939 and reached US shelves in 1948 [1]. The Norelco brand arose from a trademark dispute with Philco in the early 1940s, settled by a 1943 ruling [1]. Philips kept the Norelco name for personal care after acquiring Philco in 1981 and co-branded shavers Philips Norelco in 2005 [1]. It also acquired Schick in 1982, and Remington settled a lawsuit against Norelco in 1983 [1].
The brand's shavers range from rotary shavers to travel razors and the Bodygroom for body hair [1]. The brand name also covered non-grooming products such as video cameras and tape recorders [1].
Shaving and body-hair grooming are recurring topics in fitness and bodybuilding forums, including T Nation threads on body hair shaving and waxing and on shaving products [2][3].

timeline.event: Court ruling leads Philips to use the Norelco name in the US. [1]
